summary: Platts NE Asia PP yarn/inj rose on firm feedstock and tightening supply
China prompt premiums up on port congestion ahead of Golden Week
Petrochina/Jinneng offers to Vietnam 1,320-1,340 CIF; north traders lift offers
paras: According to Platts assessments released today, September 17, in Northeast Asia the general price level for PP yarn/injection grades rose USD 30/tonne this week from the previous week. In Southeast Asia, PP prices rose more strongly, with PP yarn/injection up USD 80/tonne to USD 1,330/tonne/CFR, BOPP up USD 80/tonne to USD 1,350/tonne/CFR, PP block copolymer also up USD 80/tonne to USD 1,380/tonne/CFR, and IPP film up USD 110/tonne to USD 1,410/tonne/CFR…

The Asian PP market continued to rise sharply this week, supported by higher feedstock prices and tightening supply. With oil prices anchored at a high level of nearly USD 110/barrel, petrochemical feedstock costs rose in tandem, eroding resin producers' profit margins; many PP producers carried out planned maintenance or cut output, further limiting supply.

Moreover, in China's export market, price premiums for prompt-delivery cargoes rose considerably due to port congestion ahead of the Golden Week holiday in early October. On the demand side, buying activity was largely confined to as-needed purchases amid continuously rising prices.

Back in the Vietnamese market, some sources said Korean PP is now less competitive and producers are no longer undercutting prices in Vietnam, as the country's exporters have recently been shipping more to Europe at higher prices. Continuously rising prices and market supply tightness have shifted buying sentiment: some buyers have accepted purchases at higher prices, believing prices will stay high or keep rising in the short term rather than cool immediately. Other market sources said Lotte Chemical Korea's PP cargo offered to Vietnam in the middle of last week had sold out.

Import offers for PP yarn/injection and BOPP of Petrochina and Jinneng (China) origin to Vietnam rose this week to USD 1,320-1,340/tonne/CIF; Jinneng's PP copolymer offers rose to USD 1,350-1,360/tonne/CIF… Other import offers were fairly sparse. Russia's Sibur PP yarn was quoted at VND 38,000-38,500/kg including VAT at Hai Phong port, though Sibur's distributor said their volumes were very small and were prioritized for regular customers to maintain the relationship rather than offered widely.

Domestically, Nghi Son Refinery and Petrochemical LLC (NSRP) opened spot sales of nearly 2,500 tonnes of PP resin, grade NSY104G/raffia fiber 4.5, for delivery from September 22-25, 2026, raising its total offered volume for September so far to about 10,500 tonnes, slightly down from the previous month's offered volume (12,000 tonnes).

In the market, after pausing over the past two days, a survey today found PP offer prices rising again. Accordingly, in the north, many traders offered NSRP's PP yarn 114G at VND 41,000/kg including VAT, up VND 500-700/kg from the start of the week; and offered BSR's PP yarn T3034 at VND 41,500/kg including VAT…

In the south, BSR's PP yarn T3034 and Hyosung Vina's PP yarn/injection were offered by traders at VND 41,000-41,200/kg including VAT, in limited volumes. Offers for Hyosung Vina's PP block copolymer and some imported grades were also pushed up to VND 42,000-42,500/kg including VAT. Other PP grades saw a similar adjustment trend, from flat to higher versus the start of the week…

“Feedstock price levels have risen too high relative to what finished-goods producers can bear, but as long as oil prices remain anchored high as they are now, PP resin prices are unlikely to cool in September,” a southern source analyzed.

summary: Sabic LLDPE film 1,330-1,360; Shenhua coal LLDPE 1,280+ CIF (Oct)
CPA US LDPE Film 1,340 CFR; spot scarce as sellers locked profits early
LSP office lifted CP Chem Singapore HDPE blow 5502 to ~VND 42,000/kg
paras: Today, September 17, Lotte Titan Malaysia announced settled PE sale prices for October 2026-delivery cargoes to Vietnamese buyers, just one day after offering. Accordingly, settled prices for Titan's LDPE grades were all USD 30/tonne below yesterday's offers, with LDPE Film 260GG settled at USD 1,550/tonne/CIF and LDPE coating 801YY settled at USD 1,650/tonne/CIF… The distributor said volumes were very small and were therefore prioritized for processing buyers.

Meanwhile, PTT of Thailand's distributor did not offer PE widely to the Vietnamese market this week; however, for buyers who inquired, PTT quoted LDPE Film sharply higher at USD 1,650/tonne/CIF, HDPE at USD 1,500/tonne/CIF, and LLDPE injection at USD 1,470/tonne/CIF… up sharply by USD 130-150/tonne from the previous week.

According to sources, PTT had sold nearly all of its October volume and in fact had little material left. Moreover, last week many Vietnamese customers had closed purchases of PTT's LDPE Film at USD 1,520/tonne/CIF, PTT's HDPE yarn at USD 1,350/tonne/CIF, and PTT's LLDPE injection at USD 1,320/tonne/CIF… so with PTT's excessively high offers this week, deals will be hard to come by.

For Chinese material, today some distributors offered coal-based LLDPE Film 7042 and 7050 of Shenhua (China) origin to Vietnam at USD 1,280-1,300/tonne/CIF; and offered oil-based LLDPE Film 7042 of Huatai and ZPC at USD 1,370-1,390/tonne/CIF, inclusive of CIC, for September-October 2026 delivery. These offers were up sharply from the start of the week and well above buyers' expectations (most buyers were still only bidding below USD 1,300/tonne/CIF for oil-based Chinese LLDPE Film)…

Middle Eastern-origin PE offers were also more numerous this week, but mostly scattered offers from trading distributors or material re-exported from China, for October-November 2026 delivery. Among these, October-delivery LLDPE Film was offered about USD 20/tonne higher than November-delivery material.

For example, one distributor offered Saudi Arabia's Sabic LLDPE film grades at USD 1,330-1,360/tonne/CIF for October delivery (November-delivery offers at USD 1,310-1,340/tonne/CIF depending on grade); and Sabic's HDPE Film at USD 1,350-1,370/tonne/CIF. Equate Kuwait's LLDPE Film was offered at USD 1,300-1,320/tonne/CIF, and Equate's HDPE Film 6888 at USD 1,380-1,395/tonne/CIF with an LSD of October 25, 2026; Qatar's Qatofin LDPE Film at USD 1,600/tonne/CIF for November delivery; and Marlex's HDPE Film at USD 1,350-1,370/tonne/CIF and Marlex's HDPE blow at USD 1,370-1,390/tonne/CIF, for October delivery…

For US material, the distributor for Channel Prime Alliance (CPA) offered LDPE Film to Vietnam at USD 1,340/tonne/CFR, and also offered HDPE Film grades at USD 1,160/tonne/CFR, with 2 containers per grade and an ETD in mid-October 2026. Although CPA's HDPE offers this week were up about USD 50/tonne from the previous week, these were still considered fairly attractive relative to the general market level. Even so, US material is far-forward and may not arrive until January 2027…

Domestically, today some traders continued to raise offers for spot LLDPE Film, especially Middle Eastern-origin grades. In the north, for example, Qamar's LLDPE Film FD21HS and Sabic's 218WJ saw some sellers offering up to VND 44,000-45,000/kg including VAT; Chinese-origin LLDPE Film was offered up to VND 41,000-42,000/kg including VAT…

“When LLDPE Film prices rose to VND 39,000-40,000/kg including VAT in early September, many traders actively sold to lock in profits. By the time prices reached VND 41,000/kg including VAT, remaining spot inventories at trading warehouses had become very scarce, while imported cargoes were arriving very slowly. This drove LLDPE prices further up to VND 44,000-45,000/kg including VAT, beyond what most market participants had forecast in early September,” a source analyzed.

For HDPE, offers also trended higher. For example, LSP's office offered CP Chem Singapore-origin HDPE blow 5502 sharply higher at VND 42,000/kg including VAT, up by as much as VND 3,200/kg from the middle of last week. HDPE Film/yarn/injection grades were also commonly offered in the VND 41,000-45,000/kg including VAT range.

As for LDPE, LDPE Film grades of PTT (Thailand), Lotte Titan and Petlin (Malaysia), Saudi Arabia's Sabic, Borouge (UAE)… were offered sharply higher by northern traders, to VND 46,000-47,000/kg including VAT; Lotte Korea's LDPE Film 512 was offered at VND 45,500/kg including VAT. US-origin LDPE Film was also offered up to VND 41,000-42,000/kg including VAT…

Across the wider region, according to Platts assessments released today, in Northeast Asia the general price level for HDPE Film/yarn/injection/blow rose USD 30/tonne this week, while LLDPE and LDPE both rose USD 20/tonne from the previous week. In Southeast Asia, HDPE grades rose USD 20/tonne this week to USD 1,260-1,270/tonne/CFR, LLDPE Film rose USD 20/tonne to USD 1,310/tonne/CFR, mLLDPE C6 rose USD 20/tonne to USD 1,360/tonne/CFR, and LDPE rose USD 20/tonne to USD 1,620/tonne/CFR…

Asia's PE market continued to draw support from a firm upstream market and reduced supply pressure. In China, some plants halted for maintenance or delayed restarts amid excessively high feedstock costs. Trading activity picked up somewhat on demand to produce finished goods ahead of the October Golden Week holiday. Southeast Asia remained under pressure from competitive import offers but faced high freight costs. Plastics converters and manufacturers bought only on an as-needed basis for immediate production rather than building inventories…

summary: Dalian PVC futures fell from 757 late last week but exports stay high
Freight/container costs keep China CIF offers elevated to Vietnam
Japanese suspension PVC 860 CFR; domestic coal SG-5 VND 22,900-23,000/kg
paras: PVC futures on the Dalian exchange (China) have fallen steadily since the start of this week, from USD 757/tonne late last week (September 11) to USD 725/tonne today (September 17), a drop of USD 32/tonne. Domestic PVC demand in China is recovering as downstream industries gradually enter their peak season, but the pace of improvement remains slow; at the same time, India's restrictions on low-priced PVC imports have reduced China's export headroom (China's PVC exports to India in August 2026 reached 11,285 tonnes, down 31% from July).

Even so, across the wider Asian market, PVC prices in most regions still rose this week. According to Platts assessments released today, September 17, the general PVC price level in China this week held flat from the previous week at USD 850/tonne/CFR, while PVC prices in Southeast Asia rose USD 15/tonne to USD 805/tonne/CFR. Market participants said ethylene-based (oil-based) PVC continued to draw support from high feedstock costs, while carbide-based (coal-based) PVC came under pressure from falling Chinese domestic prices and coal supply that is no longer as scarce as it was a few weeks earlier.

Although PVC prices in China have fallen, PVC export prices from China to Vietnam remained high due to elevated freight rates (freight for PVC from China to Vietnam is currently reported by many suppliers at USD 40-50/tonne, whereas under normal conditions it is only about USD 20-30/tonne). As a result, import offer levels for coal-based SG-5 PVC of Chinese origin to Vietnam this week were mostly USD 790-795/tonne, and Chinese-origin oil-based PVC USD 820-840/tonne/CIF, up from the previous week…

Today, September 17, SCG of Thailand's distributor offered October 2026-delivery PVC to the Vietnamese market, among the earliest producers in the region to quote October PVC. Accordingly, its SG660 PVC grade was offered at USD 850/tonne/CIF, with settled prices for some large customers recorded at USD 845/tonne/CIF; while SP660 PVC was offered at USD 841/tonne/CIF, with some large customers quoted a possible settlement at USD 837/tonne/CIF… SCG of Thailand's PVC offers this month were thus USD 25/tonne higher than the previous month.
From market sources, a Japanese producer offered suspension-grade PVC to Vietnam at USD 860/tonne/CFR, while Korean material was offered at a low of USD 790/tonne/CFR…

Domestically, midweek one leading PVC distributor quoted coal-based SG-5 PVC of Zhongtai and Yihua (China) origin at VND 22,900-23,000/kg including VAT, delivered at Yen Vien, Dong Anh (Hanoi), excluding freight, for delivery in 3-4 weeks. This offer was up VND 600/kg from early September. In the market, many traders also quickly raised their offers for coal-based Chinese SG-5 PVC to VND 23,300-23,500/kg including VAT in the north…

For oil-based PVC, some distributors continued to raise prices. However, as noted, domestic PVC inventories are high, and some traders holding large stocks contracted the previous month adjusted their prices less than other distributors, widening the gap between offer prices.

For example, for oil-based SE950/SE1000 PVC of US Shintech origin and some Southeast Asian oil-based PVC grades, the major distributor Stavian offered up to VND 25,000/kg including VAT. However, a leading trading distributor in the north offered oil-based PVC of the AGC Group (such as Thailand's Vinythai, Indonesia's Asahimas and Vietnam's AGC Vina) at VND 23,900-24,000/kg including VAT…
